summary: Frontend-only verification of Rest Timer modal cutoff fix. Opened the modal at 6 viewport sizes (375x600, 375x667, 390x844, 412x915, 768x1024, 1000x800) via Date.getDay override to force Thursday training day and clicked open-rest-timer. Programmatically asserted getBoundingClientRect containment for every required element (rest-timer-close, rest-timer-remaining, rest-timer-decrease, rest-timer-toggle, rest-timer-increase, 'Target: Ns' label, and the modal card). ALL elements fully inside viewport on ALL 6 sizes. Functional flow verified: Pause -> text changes to Resume and remaining freezes; Resume -> text changes back to Pause; +15s -> Target: 75s; -15s twice -> Target: 45s; X button closes modal; backdrop click closes modal. Initial countdown shows 1:00. No regressions.
critical_code_review_comments: RestTimer.jsx is clean and focused (~136 lines). Safe-area env() padding + items-center + max-h-full overflow-y-auto correctly resolves the mobile bottom-anchor cutoff. No issues.
seed_data_creation: None - used Date.prototype.getDay override to force Thursday (training day) so open-rest-timer button was reachable on Today screen.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Rest Timer modal viewport containment + functional behavior verified across mobile (375x600, 375x667, 390x844, 412x915), tablet (768x1024), and desktop (1000x800). The Date.getDay=4 init script trick is required to unlock the open-rest-timer button on Today, since the seeded test environment defaults to Wednesday rest day.
rca of the issue: Original bug RCA (already fixed by main agent, confirmed in this iteration): modal used items-end on mobile which stuck it to the bottom of the viewport, where mobile browser chrome (Safari URL bar / home indicator) overlapped the -15s/Pause/+15s row and the 'Target: 60s' label. Fix: switched to items-center at all breakpoints, added max(1rem, env(safe-area-inset-top/bottom)) padding on the overlay, capped modal card at max-h-full with overflow-y-auto, and tightened mobile spacing/type scale. Verified boundingClientRect.bottom <= innerHeight on shortest viewport (375x600).
